summary: Three of us at the co-working space, plus one teammate on Zoom from California. We ordered takeout: Thai, wraps, salads. Terri kicked things off with an activity to get us going, then we got into ideas for the Replit buildathon. We talked through a few: an ethical terms-and-conditions app, a tool to help international students with visa stuff, an ethical rideshare service. The T&C app got the most traction. The idea is that it would track updated terms across App Store apps and let users flag clauses that look sketchy before accepting. We spent most of the session digging into that one.

Morning at Back 9. None of us had really played golf before. Leilani and her friend picked the games, and the rules changed each round so we mostly just figured it out as we went. Different people won different games, which made it feel more fun than competitive. We had nachos, cheese curds, and jalapeño poppers.

Lunch at Bosphorus Cafe. Terri shared news on a couple of fronts: she's heading to Greece soon to present her paper on the AGAIN mindset, and she's going to a CEO retreat in Chicago next week. The conversation drifted into food spots in Indy and Hawaii, then into scuba, snorkeling, surfing, and shark stories. Vaishnava and Terri got into Spartan races and triathlons. The eggplant salsa and baklava were the standouts.

blurbs.name: Terri
blurbs.text: I could see the sea floor in Hawaii. Turtles. One shark.

blurbs.name: Agrima
blurbs.text: Once held an octopus underwater. Wouldn't recommend.

blurbs.name: Anushka
blurbs.text: Dead lobster, malfunctioning helmet, the whole thing was a lot.

blurbs.name: Vaishnava
blurbs.text: My scuba dive video has more fish in post-production than I saw in real life.

summary: For May we hit Axum, an Ethiopian place with art on every wall and hand drawn sketches on each table. Vaishnava, Terri, Aileen, and Leilani came, and the room won everyone over before the food even arrived. Between bites we mapped out Aileen's upcoming Puerto Rico trip and somehow landed on FIFA. The table gave it a 9 for vibe, a 9 for food, and an 8.5 overall.

blurbs.name: Terri
blurbs.text: The hand drawn pencil sketches on every table got me, each one different. I kept getting distracted from the menu.

blurbs.name: Leilani
blurbs.text: We spent a good chunk of lunch geeking out over Aileen's Puerto Rico trip next weekend, throwing out every spot we could think of. Planning someone else's vacation is weirdly fun.

blurbs.name: Aileen
blurbs.text: Vaishnava and I were the two who went for the Ethiopian coffee. Strong, with a real cardamom kick. We asked for sugar and got a knowing smirk from the owner, which was fair.

blurbs.name: Vaishnava
blurbs.text: The owner checking under our table for his hiding kid before we sat down. That little thing is what made the place feel like home.

favoriteThing: Terri's camera tour of Oahu at sunrise
summary: Four of us on Zoom across three time zones. Terri was in Hawaii at her parents' house on Oahu, where it was 5:30 in the morning and pitch dark when we started and full daylight by the time we got off. She sent everyone gift cards so lunch was on the company. It started as a round of what is the newest thing you learned and turned into an hour of Hawaii geography, complete with a camera tour of her parents' yard and a shared map.

blurbs.name: Terri
blurbs.text: There are eight islands, and the whole chain came from one hot spot in the middle of the Pacific. The plate keeps sliding northwest, so the islands get older and smaller the further up you go. I grew up learning this in geography class. Meanwhile I still could not name the states around Indiana.

blurbs.name: Aileen
blurbs.text: I decided last minute to go get Cava, added the gift card to my wallet, and just hoped for the best. Worst comes to worst I pay. Also I genuinely thought Hawaii was one island until Terri started moving around the map and I went, wait, where are we going?

blurbs.name: Anushka
blurbs.text: I tried to order Chick-fil-A at 9:56 and they told me they were closing in four minutes. So I sat on the call with no food for half an hour and got Panda Express after.

blurbs.name: Vaishnava
blurbs.text: I looked at Cava, did the math, and the tax on one meal was more than the meal itself. Got Bazbeaux later instead. Then Terri turned her camera around and there were mountains behind the house and the ocean across the street, and I stopped thinking about lunch.

summary: Five of us at Hyderabad House, and it turned into the most Indian lunch we have had. The Karampodi Gobi came out first and disappeared fastest, spicy and crisp and the thing everyone kept reaching for, with the chicken lollipops close behind and Leilani's pick of the day. After that came butter garlic naan, malai kofta, and the Vijayawada special chicken biryani, which was very close to stealing the show. Somewhere between the biryani and dessert the table turned into a conversation about home. Vaishnava is from Hyderabad, Agrima from Bombay, Anushka from Delhi, and most of it came back to street food, momos, and how easy it is to eat well for almost nothing on an Indian street. Then Bollywood. Terri has seen Baahubali, so we spent a while deciding what she should watch next and landed somewhere between RRR and Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham. Dessert was gulab jamun ice cream, which everyone liked, and paan ice cream, which Terri tried once and did not go back to. Leilani spent the meal shooting gifs, memes and food photos for the post, so this is the best documented lunch on the passport.
